3-1.title: Pronoun Case (Subject vs. Object)
3-1.learn:
HOW TO CHOOSE SUBJECT VS. OBJECT PRONOUNS

SUBJECT pronouns DO the action: I, he, she, we, they, who.
OBJECT pronouns RECEIVE the action or follow a preposition (to, for, with): me, him, her, us, them, whom.

Example 1 — 'She gave the ball to me.'
'She' is the subject (doing the giving). 'Me' is the object (receiving the action after 'to'). Correct!

Example 2 — Wrong: 'Her gave the ball to I.'
'Her' cannot be the subject, and 'I' cannot be the object. Fix: 'She gave the ball to me.'

Example 3 — The 'remove the other person' trick: 'Maria and (I/me) went to the park.'
Take out 'Maria and': you would say 'I went to the park,' not 'Me went.' So choose 'I': 'Maria and I went to the park.'
For 'The teacher called Sam and (I/me),' remove 'Sam and': 'The teacher called me,' so choose 'me.'

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: '___ ran to the store.'
questions.explanation: The pronoun is doing the action (running), so a subject pronoun like 'She' is correct.

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'Dad drove ___ to school.'
questions.explanation: The pronoun receives the action (being driven), so the object pronoun 'me' is correct.

questions.question: Which is a SUBJECT pronoun?
questions.explanation: 'They' is a subject pronoun that does the action; the others are object pronouns.

questions.explanation: After the preposition 'to,' use the object pronoun 'them.'

questions.explanation: Remove 'Sam and': you would say 'picked me,' so the object pronoun 'me' is correct.

questions.explanation: Both pronouns are subjects doing the action, so use 'He and I.'

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'Between you and ___, this is a secret.'
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'between,' use the object pronoun 'me': 'between you and me.'

questions.explanation: The students are doing the action, so the subject pronoun 'We' is correct.

questions.explanation: The pronoun is the subject doing the walking, so the subject pronoun 'He' is correct.

questions.explanation: The pronoun is the subject doing the baking, so the subject pronoun 'She' is correct.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: The subject doing the action needs a subject pronoun, so 'We' is correct.

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'Grandma and ___ baked a pie together.'
questions.explanation: Remove 'Grandma and': you would say 'I baked,' so the subject pronoun 'I' is correct.

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'The principal thanked the teachers and ___.'

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'The waiter brought the menus to my mom and ___.'
questions.explanation: Remove 'my mom and': you would say 'brought to me,' so the object pronoun 'me' is correct.

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'My brother and ___ share a room.'
questions.explanation: Remove 'My brother and': you would say 'I share,' so the subject pronoun 'I' is correct.

questions.explanation: In a comparison, the full thought is 'faster than she is,' so the subject pronoun 'she' is correct.

questions.explanation: The pronoun receives the action (being chosen), so the object pronoun 'us' is correct.

questions.explanation: Remove 'the twins and': you would say 'for me,' so the object pronoun 'me' is correct.

choices.B: She and he are coming over.

choices.D: She and him are coming over.

3-2.title: Pronoun-Antecedent Agreement
3-2.learn:
HOW TO MAKE PRONOUNS AGREE WITH THEIR ANTECEDENTS

An ANTECEDENT is the noun a pronoun replaces. A pronoun must MATCH its antecedent in number (singular/plural) and gender (he/she/it).

Example 1 — 'The dog wagged its tail.'
Antecedent = 'dog' (singular). Pronoun = 'its' (singular). They match.

Example 2 — 'The students raised their hands.'
Antecedent = 'students' (plural). Pronoun = 'their' (plural). They match.

Example 3 — Watch singular antecedents: 'Each student raised his or her hand.'
Words like 'each,' 'every,' 'everyone,' 'someone,' and 'anybody' are SINGULAR, so they take a singular pronoun ('his or her'), not 'their.'
Wrong: 'Everyone brought their lunch.' Better (singular match): 'Everyone brought his or her lunch.'

Tip: First find the noun the pronoun stands for. Decide if it is singular or plural, then pick a matching pronoun.

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'The cat licked ___ fur.'
questions.explanation: The singular antecedent 'cat' takes the singular pronoun 'its.'

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'The players grabbed ___ jerseys.'
questions.explanation: The plural antecedent 'players' takes the plural pronoun 'their.'

questions.explanation: An antecedent is the noun that a pronoun stands for or replaces.

questions.explanation: The singular, female antecedent 'Maria' takes the pronoun 'her.'

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'Neither of the boys brought ___ lunch.'
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular and refers to the boys, so it takes the singular masculine pronoun 'his.'

questions.question: Which sentence has correct agreement?

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'The choir sang ___ best song last.'

3-3.title: Fixing Vague Pronoun References
3-3.learn:
HOW TO FIX VAGUE PRONOUN REFERENCES

Every pronoun ('he,' 'she,' 'it,' 'they,' 'this') should clearly point to ONE noun. If a reader cannot tell exactly who or what the pronoun means, the reference is VAGUE and confusing.

Example 1 — Vague: 'Maya told Lily that she won.'
Who won — Maya or Lily? 'She' is unclear. Fix by naming the person: 'Maya told Lily, "You won!"' or 'Maya told Lily that Lily won.'

Example 2 — Vague 'it': 'I put the book on the shelf, but it broke.'
What broke — the book or the shelf? Fix: 'I put the book on the shelf, but the shelf broke.'

Example 3 — Vague 'they': 'They say exercise is good for you.'
Who is 'they'? Fix: 'Doctors say exercise is good for you.'

To fix vague pronouns: replace the pronoun with the exact noun, or rewrite the sentence so only one noun could possibly match.

questions.question: Why is this sentence unclear? 'Jake told Ben that he made a mistake.'
questions.explanation: The pronoun 'he' could refer to either Jake or Ben, making the reference vague.

questions.question: Which sentence has a CLEAR pronoun reference?

choices.A: Sara told Mia that she was late.
choices.B: When the dog saw the cat, it ran.
choices.D: I dropped the plate on the table, and it cracked.

questions.explanation: By using direct words ('You are late'), it is clear that Mia is the one who is late.

questions.question: What does a vague pronoun do to a sentence?

choices.B: Confuses the reader about who or what is meant

questions.explanation: A vague pronoun makes it unclear which noun is meant, confusing the reader.

questions.question: Which is the BEST fix for: 'I set the cup on the plate, and it broke.'?

choices.A: I set the cup on the plate, and the plate broke.
choices.B: I set it on the plate, and it broke.
choices.C: I set the cup on it, and it broke.

questions.explanation: Replacing the vague 'it' with 'the plate' makes clear which object broke.

questions.question: Which sentence has a VAGUE pronoun?

choices.B: The bird flew to its nest.
choices.C: When Lee met Sam, he smiled.

questions.explanation: 'He' could mean Lee or Sam, so the reference is vague.

questions.question: Which is the BEST fix for: 'Anna told Beth that she had won the award.'?

choices.A: Anna told Beth that she had won.
choices.B: Anna told Beth, "You have won the award."
choices.C: She told her that she had won.

questions.explanation: Using direct words makes clear that Beth is the winner, removing the vague 'she.'

questions.question: Why is 'They closed the school early' vague if no one was named before?

choices.A: 'They' has no clear antecedent — we don't know who 'they' is.

questions.explanation: Without a noun earlier in the sentence, 'they' has no clear antecedent and is vague.

questions.question: Which revision makes the pronoun reference clear in 'The coach told the player he was proud'?

choices.A: The coach told the player he was proud.
choices.B: The coach told the player, "I am proud of you."
choices.C: He told him he was proud.
choices.D: The coach told him he was proud.

questions.explanation: Using direct words makes clear that the coach is the proud one, fixing the vague 'he.'

questions.question: Which sentence has NO vague pronoun problem?

choices.A: After Maria called Lily, she felt better.
choices.B: When the teacher handed the student the test, she looked nervous.
choices.C: The chef placed the pan on the stove, and it got hot.
choices.D: After the storm passed, the children went outside.

questions.explanation: In choice D, every reference is clear; the others leave 'she' or 'it' pointing to more than one noun.

questions.question: What is the BEST way to fix a vague pronoun?

choices.B: Replace the pronoun with the exact noun it means.

questions.explanation: Replacing a vague pronoun with the specific noun makes the meaning clear.

questions.question: Why is this sentence unclear? 'Carlos told Diego that he had won.'
questions.explanation: The pronoun 'he' could refer to either Carlos or Diego, making it vague.

questions.question: Which sentence has a CLEAR pronoun reference?

choices.A: Lily told Grace that she was sick.
choices.B: The dog chased the squirrel until it got tired.
choices.C: After the bell rang, the students lined up at the door.
choices.D: Tom told Jim that he forgot his book.

questions.explanation: In choice C there is no confusing pronoun; every reference is clear.

questions.question: A pronoun should clearly point to how many nouns?
questions.explanation: A clear pronoun points to exactly one noun so the reader is never confused.

questions.question: In 'She put the vase on the table, and it cracked,' why is 'it' vague?

choices.A: 'It' could mean the vase or the table.

questions.explanation: Either the vase or the table could have cracked, so 'it' is vague.

questions.question: Which sentence has a VAGUE pronoun?

choices.A: The rabbit hopped into its hole.
choices.B: When Mia saw Kate, she waved.

questions.explanation: 'She' could mean Mia or Kate, so the reference is vague.

questions.question: What word in this sentence is vague? 'They raised the prices at the store again.'
questions.explanation: With no noun named before it, 'They' has no clear antecedent and is vague.

questions.question: Which sentence is CLEAR, not vague?

choices.A: The teacher told the boy he passed.
choices.B: Sam told Alex he was chosen.
choices.C: The hikers reached the cabin before dark.
choices.D: Mom told Sue she could go.

questions.explanation: Choice C has no confusing pronoun; the others leave 'he' or 'she' pointing to two people.

questions.question: A vague pronoun reference happens when a pronoun could point to ___ noun.
questions.explanation: A reference is vague when the pronoun could match more than one noun.

questions.question: Which sentence needs to be fixed for a vague pronoun?

choices.A: The phone fell on the keyboard, and it broke.
choices.B: The phone fell, and the screen broke.
choices.C: After Jake studied, he passed the quiz.
choices.D: The cat curled up on its bed.

questions.explanation: 'It' could mean the phone or the keyboard, so the reference is vague.

questions.question: Which sentence has a CLEAR reference?

choices.A: Ben told Will that he was right.
choices.B: When the cup hit the bowl, it shattered.
choices.D: After it rained, the streets were wet.

questions.explanation: In choice D every reference is clear; the others leave a pronoun pointing to two nouns.

questions.question: Which is the BEST fix for: 'Noah told Eli that he had made the team.'?

choices.A: Noah told Eli that he had made it.
choices.B: Noah told Eli, "You made the team!"
choices.C: He told him that he had made the team.
choices.D: Noah told Eli about the team.

questions.explanation: Using direct words makes clear that Eli made the team, removing the vague 'he.'

questions.question: Which sentence has a VAGUE pronoun?

choices.A: The bee returned to its hive.
choices.B: When the manager met the new worker, she smiled.

questions.explanation: 'She' could mean the manager or the worker, so the reference is vague.

questions.question: Which is the BEST fix for: 'I left the book on the desk, but it was dusty.'?

choices.A: I left the book on the desk, but it was dusty.
choices.B: I left it on the desk, but it was dusty.
choices.C: I left the book on the desk, but the desk was dusty.
choices.D: It was dusty on the desk.

questions.explanation: Replacing the vague 'it' with 'the desk' makes clear which thing was dusty.

questions.question: Which revision fixes the vague 'they' in 'They closed the road for repairs'?

choices.A: The city closed the road for repairs.

questions.explanation: Naming 'the city' replaces the vague 'they' with a clear noun.

questions.question: Which sentence has NO vague pronoun?

choices.A: When Ana texted Beth, she laughed.
choices.B: The ball hit the window, and it shattered.
choices.C: The runners crossed the finish line together.
choices.D: Lee told Pat that he was tired.

questions.explanation: Choice C has no confusing pronoun; the others leave 'she,' 'it,' or 'he' pointing to two nouns.

questions.question: Which is the BEST fix for: 'My brother told my dad that his car needed gas.'?

choices.A: My brother told my dad that his car needed gas.
choices.B: My brother told my dad, "Your car needs gas."
choices.C: He told him that his car needed gas.
choices.D: My brother told my dad about gas.

questions.explanation: Using direct words shows that dad's car needs gas, removing the vague 'his.'

questions.question: Why is 'In the report, it says sleep is important' weak?

choices.A: 'It' has no clear noun to refer to.

questions.explanation: 'It' refers to nothing specific; better: 'The report says sleep is important.'

questions.question: Which sentence has a VAGUE pronoun?

choices.B: When the doctor saw the nurse, he nodded.

questions.explanation: 'He' could mean the doctor or the nurse, so the reference is vague.

questions.question: Which is the BEST fix for: 'The plate fell on the cup, and it cracked.'?

choices.A: The plate fell on the cup, and the cup cracked.
choices.B: It fell on the cup, and it cracked.
choices.C: The plate fell on it, and it cracked.

questions.explanation: Replacing 'it' with 'the cup' makes clear which object cracked.

questions.question: Which sentence keeps the reference clear?

choices.A: Jordan told Riley that he won the contest.
choices.B: Jordan told Riley, "I won the contest."
choices.C: He told him that he won the contest.

questions.explanation: Using direct words makes clear that Jordan won, fixing the vague 'he.'

questions.question: Which revision BEST fixes the vague pronoun in 'When the singer met the dancer, she bowed'?

choices.A: When the singer met the dancer, she bowed.
choices.B: When the singer met the dancer, the dancer bowed.
choices.C: When she met her, she bowed.
choices.D: When the singer met her, she bowed.

questions.explanation: Naming 'the dancer' removes the vague 'she' and shows exactly who bowed.

questions.question: Which sentence has NO vague pronoun problem?

choices.A: After Lena called Rosa, she felt relieved.
choices.B: When the chef greeted the waiter, he smiled.
choices.C: The cup slid into the bowl, and it broke.
choices.D: Once the bell rang, the class hurried to lunch.

questions.explanation: In choice D every reference is clear; the others leave 'she,' 'he,' or 'it' pointing to two nouns.

questions.question: Which is the BEST fix for: 'Maria told her sister that she had to leave.'?

choices.A: Maria told her sister, "You have to leave."
choices.B: Maria told her sister that she had to go.
choices.C: She told her that she had to leave.
choices.D: Maria told her sister about leaving.

questions.explanation: Direct words make clear that the sister has to leave, removing the vague 'she.'

questions.question: What makes 'They give out awards at the ceremony' unclear?
questions.explanation: Without naming who gives the awards, 'They' has no clear antecedent.

questions.question: Which revision makes the reference clear in 'The author thanked the editor for her work'?

choices.A: The author thanked the editor, saying, "Your work was excellent."
choices.B: The author thanked the editor for her work.
choices.C: She thanked her for her work.
choices.D: The author thanked her for it.

questions.explanation: Direct words show that the editor's work is meant, fixing the vague 'her.'

questions.question: Which sentence is the CLEAREST?

choices.A: When the bird saw the cat, it flew away.
choices.B: When the bird saw the cat, the bird flew away.
choices.C: It flew away when it saw it.
choices.D: When it saw the cat, it flew away.

questions.explanation: Naming 'the bird' removes any doubt about which animal flew away.

questions.question: Which is the BEST fix for: 'I read the letter and the card, but it was kind.'?

choices.A: I read the letter and the card, but the card was kind.
choices.B: I read them, but it was kind.
choices.C: I read it, but it was kind.
choices.D: It was kind to read them.

questions.explanation: Replacing 'it' with 'the card' makes clear which item was kind.

questions.question: Which sentence has a vague pronoun that should be fixed?

choices.A: After the coach praised the captain, he grinned.
choices.B: After the coach praised the captain, the captain grinned.
choices.C: After the rain stopped, the field dried.
choices.D: The dog wagged its tail happily.

questions.explanation: 'He' could mean the coach or the captain, so this reference is vague.

questions.question: Which revision clears up 'Sara emailed Nina before she went on vacation'?

choices.A: Sara emailed Nina before Sara went on vacation.
choices.B: Sara emailed Nina before she went on vacation.
choices.C: She emailed her before she left.

questions.explanation: Naming 'Sara' shows who went on vacation, fixing the vague 'she.'

questions.question: Which sentence avoids a vague pronoun BEST?

choices.A: The ladder leaned against the wall, and it was tall.
choices.B: The ladder leaned against the wall, and the wall was tall.
choices.C: It leaned against it, and it was tall.
choices.D: The ladder leaned against it, and it was tall.

questions.explanation: Naming 'the wall' makes clear which object was tall, avoiding the vague 'it.'

3-4.title: Pronoun Person (Staying Consistent)
3-4.learn:
HOW TO STAY CONSISTENT IN PRONOUN PERSON

There are three 'persons' in writing:
FIRST person = I, me, we, us (the writer/speaker).
SECOND person = you (the reader).
THIRD person = he, she, it, they, one (someone else).
Pick one point of view and STICK with it. Don't switch in the middle.

Example 1 — Inconsistent: 'When a player practices, you improve.'
This switches from third person ('a player') to second person ('you'). Fix by matching: 'When players practice, they improve.' (third person throughout) OR 'When you practice, you improve.' (second person throughout).

Example 2 — Inconsistent: 'I love hiking because you get fresh air.'
This jumps from first person ('I') to second person ('you'). Fix: 'I love hiking because I get fresh air.'

Example 3 — Consistent: 'Students should bring their books so they are ready.'
Everything stays in third person, so it reads smoothly.

To check: underline every pronoun. If they jump between I, you, and he/they for the SAME subject, make them match.

questions.question: Which sentence keeps pronoun person CONSISTENT?

choices.A: When a student studies, you do better.
choices.B: When I study, you do better.
choices.C: When a student studies, we do better.
choices.D: When students study, they do better.

questions.explanation: Both 'students' and 'they' are third person, so the sentence stays consistent.

questions.question: Which pronouns are FIRST person?
questions.explanation: First-person pronouns refer to the writer or speaker: I, we, us, me.

questions.question: Which sentence switches point of view incorrectly?

choices.A: When I exercise, I feel great.
choices.B: When you exercise, you feel great.
choices.C: When I exercise, you feel great.
choices.D: When they exercise, they feel great.

questions.explanation: Choice C jumps from first person 'I' to second person 'you' for the same idea.

questions.question: Fix the shift: 'If a person wants to win, ___ must practice.'
questions.explanation: To match the third-person 'a person,' use 'they' (treated as singular here) rather than switching to 'you.'

questions.question: Which revision keeps the pronoun person consistent: 'I enjoy reading because you learn new things.'?

choices.A: I enjoy reading because you learn new things.
choices.B: I enjoy reading because I learn new things.
choices.C: You enjoy reading because I learn new things.
choices.D: We enjoy reading because you learn new things.

questions.explanation: Keeping 'I' in both parts makes the sentence consistently first person.

questions.question: Which sentence is consistent in second person?

choices.A: You should wear a helmet so they stay safe.
choices.B: You should wear a helmet so you stay safe.
choices.C: You should wear a helmet so I stay safe.
choices.D: One should wear a helmet so you stay safe.

questions.explanation: Both pronouns are 'you,' keeping the sentence in consistent second person.

questions.question: Which pronoun is THIRD person?
questions.explanation: 'They' refers to other people and is a third-person pronoun.

questions.question: Which sentence has a point-of-view shift that should be fixed?

choices.A: Swimmers should stretch before they dive in.
choices.B: If you want strong muscles, one must lift weights.
choices.C: We packed our bags before we left.
choices.D: She finished her project on time.

questions.explanation: Choice B shifts from second person 'you' to third person 'one' for the same idea.

questions.question: Which is the BEST consistent revision of 'When a driver is tired, you should rest'?

choices.A: When a driver is tired, he or she should rest.
choices.B: When a driver is tired, you should rest.
choices.C: When a driver is tired, we should rest.
choices.D: When a driver is tired, I should rest.

questions.explanation: Matching the third-person 'a driver' with 'he or she' keeps the point of view consistent.

questions.question: Which paragraph keeps the point of view consistent throughout?

choices.A: I love camping. You get to see stars, and we cook over a fire.
choices.B: You love camping. I get to see stars, and they cook over a fire.
choices.C: We love camping. You get to see stars, and I cook over a fire.
choices.D: I love camping. I get to see stars, and I cook over a fire.

questions.explanation: Every sentence stays in first person ('I'), so the point of view is consistent.

questions.question: Which sentence keeps pronoun person CONSISTENT?

choices.A: When a swimmer trains, you get stronger.
choices.B: When swimmers train, they get stronger.
choices.C: When a swimmer trains, we get stronger.
choices.D: When I train, you get stronger.

questions.explanation: Both 'swimmers' and 'they' are third person, so the sentence stays consistent.

questions.question: Which pronouns are SECOND person?
questions.explanation: Second-person pronouns refer to the reader: you and your.

questions.question: Which sentence switches point of view incorrectly?

choices.A: When we travel, we pack light.
choices.B: When you travel, you pack light.
choices.C: When we travel, you pack light.
choices.D: When they travel, they pack light.

questions.explanation: Choice C jumps from first person 'we' to second person 'you' for the same idea.

questions.question: Which pronoun is FIRST person?
questions.explanation: 'We' refers to the writer and others, so it is a first-person pronoun.

questions.question: Which sentence keeps point of view CONSISTENT?

choices.A: You should eat well so I feel good.
choices.B: You should eat well so you feel good.
choices.C: You should eat well so they feel good.
choices.D: You should eat well so we feel good.

questions.explanation: Both pronouns are 'you,' keeping the sentence in consistent second person.

questions.question: Which pronoun is SECOND person?
questions.explanation: 'You' refers to the reader, so it is a second-person pronoun.

questions.question: Which sentence stays in third person throughout?

choices.A: A reader should take notes so you remember.
choices.B: Readers should take notes so they remember.
choices.C: A reader should take notes so we remember.
choices.D: I should take notes so you remember.

questions.explanation: Both 'readers' and 'they' are third person, so the sentence is consistent.

questions.question: How many 'persons' (points of view) are there in writing?
questions.explanation: There are three persons: first (I/we), second (you), and third (he/she/they).

questions.question: Which sentence switches point of view incorrectly?

choices.A: They study hard, so they earn good grades.
choices.B: We study hard, so we earn good grades.
choices.C: A student studies hard, so you earn good grades.
choices.D: You study hard, so you earn good grades.

questions.explanation: Choice C jumps from third person 'a student' to second person 'you' for the same idea.

questions.question: Which pronouns are THIRD person?
questions.explanation: Third-person pronouns refer to other people or things: he, she, it, they.

questions.question: Fix the shift: 'When a cook follows a recipe, ___ usually succeeds.'
questions.explanation: To match the third-person 'a cook,' use 'he or she,' not the second-person 'you.'

questions.question: Which revision keeps person consistent: 'We enjoy hiking because you breathe fresh air.'?

choices.A: We enjoy hiking because you breathe fresh air.
choices.B: We enjoy hiking because we breathe fresh air.
choices.C: You enjoy hiking because we breathe fresh air.
choices.D: They enjoy hiking because you breathe fresh air.

questions.explanation: Keeping 'we' in both parts makes the sentence consistently first person.

questions.question: Which sentence is consistent in third person?

choices.A: A driver should slow down so you stay safe.
choices.B: A driver should slow down so he or she stays safe.
choices.C: A driver should slow down so we stay safe.
choices.D: A driver should slow down so I stay safe.

questions.explanation: Matching 'a driver' with 'he or she' keeps the sentence in third person.

questions.question: Fix the shift: 'If students want to pass, ___ should review their notes.'
questions.explanation: To match the third-person plural 'students,' use 'they,' not 'you.'

questions.question: Which sentence keeps person consistent?

choices.A: I like soccer because you make new friends.
choices.B: I like soccer because I make new friends.
choices.C: You like soccer because I make new friends.
choices.D: We like soccer because you make new friends.

questions.explanation: Keeping 'I' in both parts makes the sentence consistently first person.

questions.question: Which revision keeps person consistent: 'A gardener waters plants daily so you get blooms.'?

choices.A: A gardener waters plants daily so you get blooms.
choices.B: A gardener waters plants daily so he or she gets blooms.
choices.C: A gardener waters plants daily so we get blooms.
choices.D: A gardener waters plants daily so I get blooms.

questions.explanation: Matching 'a gardener' with 'he or she' keeps the sentence in third person.

questions.question: Which sentence has a point-of-view shift?

choices.A: When you exercise, you sleep better.
choices.B: When we exercise, we sleep better.
choices.C: When athletes exercise, you sleep better.
choices.D: When they exercise, they sleep better.

questions.explanation: Choice C shifts from third person 'athletes' to second person 'you.'

questions.question: Fix the shift: 'I enjoy art class because ___ can be creative.'
questions.explanation: To match the first-person 'I,' use 'I,' not the second-person 'you.'

questions.question: Which sentence is consistent in first person?

choices.A: We finished our homework, then you watched a movie.
choices.B: We finished our homework, then we watched a movie.
choices.C: We finished our homework, then they watched a movie.
choices.D: You finished your homework, then we watched a movie.

questions.explanation: Both pronouns are first person ('we'), so the point of view is consistent.

questions.question: Which revision keeps person consistent: 'When you save money, one feels secure.'?

choices.A: When you save money, one feels secure.
choices.B: When you save money, you feel secure.
choices.C: When you save money, they feel secure.
choices.D: When you save money, I feel secure.

questions.explanation: Matching 'you' with 'you' keeps the sentence in consistent second person.

questions.question: Which sentence has a point-of-view shift that should be fixed?

choices.A: Writers should revise their drafts before they submit them.
choices.B: If a hiker plans well, you avoid getting lost.
choices.C: We packed our gear before we set out.
choices.D: He practiced daily until he mastered the song.

questions.explanation: Choice B shifts from third person 'a hiker' to second person 'you' for the same idea.

questions.question: Which is the BEST consistent revision of 'When a teacher grades papers, you stay focused'?

choices.A: When a teacher grades papers, he or she stays focused.
choices.B: When a teacher grades papers, you stay focused.
choices.C: When a teacher grades papers, we stay focused.
choices.D: When a teacher grades papers, I stay focused.

questions.explanation: Matching the third-person 'a teacher' with 'he or she' keeps the point of view consistent.

questions.question: Which paragraph keeps point of view consistent?

choices.A: We love the beach. You build castles, and they swim.
choices.B: You love the beach. We build castles, and I swim.
choices.C: We love the beach. We build castles, and we swim.
choices.D: I love the beach. You build castles, and we swim.

questions.explanation: Every sentence stays in first person ('we'), so the point of view is consistent.

questions.question: Which sentence shifts point of view and needs fixing?

choices.A: If one wishes to improve, one must practice.
choices.B: If one wishes to improve, you must practice.
choices.C: If you wish to improve, you must practice.
choices.D: If they wish to improve, they must practice.

questions.explanation: Choice B shifts from the third-person 'one' to the second-person 'you.'

questions.question: Which is the BEST consistent revision of 'When a chef cooks, you must taste the food'?

choices.A: When a chef cooks, he or she must taste the food.
choices.B: When a chef cooks, you must taste the food.
choices.C: When a chef cooks, we must taste the food.
choices.D: When a chef cooks, I must taste the food.

questions.explanation: Matching the third-person 'a chef' with 'he or she' keeps the point of view consistent.

questions.question: Which paragraph stays consistent in third person?

choices.A: A student opens the book. You read carefully, and they take notes.
choices.B: Students open the book. They read carefully, and they take notes.
choices.C: Students open the book. You read carefully, and we take notes.
choices.D: A student opens the book. I read carefully, and you take notes.

questions.explanation: Every sentence stays in third person ('students,' 'they'), so it is consistent.

questions.question: Which sentence keeps point of view consistent?

choices.A: When a person reads daily, you build vocabulary.
choices.B: When people read daily, they build vocabulary.
choices.C: When a person reads daily, we build vocabulary.
choices.D: When I read daily, you build vocabulary.

questions.explanation: Both 'people' and 'they' are third person, so the sentence is consistent.

questions.question: Which is the BEST consistent revision of 'When you join a team, one learns teamwork'?

choices.A: When you join a team, you learn teamwork.
choices.B: When you join a team, one learns teamwork.
choices.C: When you join a team, they learn teamwork.
choices.D: When you join a team, I learn teamwork.

questions.explanation: Matching 'you' with 'you' keeps the sentence consistently second person.

questions.question: Which sentence shifts point of view and should be fixed?

choices.A: Musicians rehearse often, so they perform well.
choices.B: I rehearse often, so I perform well.
choices.C: A musician rehearses often, so you perform well.
choices.D: You rehearse often, so you perform well.

questions.explanation: Choice C shifts from third person 'a musician' to second person 'you' for the same idea.

questions.question: Which paragraph keeps point of view consistent throughout?

choices.A: You enjoy science. I run experiments, and they record data.
choices.B: We enjoy science. You run experiments, and I record data.
choices.C: You enjoy science. You run experiments, and you record data.
choices.D: I enjoy science. We run experiments, and they record data.

questions.explanation: Every sentence stays in second person ('you'), so the point of view is consistent.
